title: कृष्ण उपन्यासमा मिथकीयता
nepali: शंकरप्रसाद गैरे नेपाली आख्यानका क्षेत्रमा उत्तरआधुनिक चिन्तनलाई अनुसरण गरी उपन्यास लेख्ने व्यक्ति हुन् । प्रस्तुत लेखमा नेपाली समालोचनाका क्षेत्रमा समसामयिक कालमा चर्चामा रहेको मिथकीय सिद्धान्तका आधारमा शंकरप्रसाद गैरेको कृष्ण उपन्यासलाई विश्लेषण गर्ने काम गरिएको छ । कृष्ण उपन्यास पौराणिक विषयलाई आधुनिक आँखाबाट हेरिएको कृति हो । उपन्यासमा पुराणका सन्दर्भका साथमा समकालीन समाजको यथार्थ अवस्थालाई प्रस्तुत गरिएको पाइन्छ । यसलाई मिथकीय सिद्धान्तका आधारबाट अध्ययन गर्नु सान्दर्भिक मानिएको छ । मिथकीय सिद्धान्त पाश्चात्य साहित्य चिन्तनमा मूलतः उत्तरआधुनिक समयमा विकास भएको एक समालोचकीय मान्यता हो । युङ्गको सामूहिक अचेतनका पृष्ठभूमिबाट अतीतका विषय र घटनाहरूको खोजी गरी विश्लेषण गर्ने काम यसले गर्दछ । शंकरप्रसाद गैरेको कृष्ण उपन्यासमा प्रयुक्त मिथकीय सन्दर्भहरूलाई पहिचान गर्नु यस लेखको प्रमुख समस्या हो । मिथकीय अवधारणामा केन्द्रित रहेर कृष्ण उपन्यासको विश्लेषण गरी निष्कर्षमा पुग्नु नै प्रस्तुत लेखको उद्देश्य हो । मिथकीय सिद्धान्तमा टेकेर कृतिको विश्लेषण गरिएको हुनाले प्रस्तुत लेखमा समालोचनाको सैद्धान्तिक विधिलाई उपयोग गरिएको छ । कृष्ण उपन्यास महाभारतकालीन आख्यानको पुनर्लेखन हो । यस उपन्यासमा प्रयुक्त विषयवस्तु, पात्र र तिनको व्यवहार पौराणिक कथाकै पृष्ठभूमिमा उठेको देखाइएको छ । पौराणिक तथा अलौकिक घटना र सन्दर्भलाई समकालीन चेतनाका आधारमा प्रस्तुत गरी घटना, पात्र र तिनका प्रवृत्तिलाई पुनर्लेखन गरिएकाले उपन्यासमा मिथकीय चेतना अनुकूल बनेर आएको देखिन्छ । प्रस्तुत लेखमा आवश्यक सामग्री प्राथमिक र द्वितीयक स्रोतबाट लिइएको छ । मिथकीय पुनव्र्याख्या तथा पुनर्लेखनलाई सैद्धान्तिक आधार बनाई आवश्यकताअनुरूप प्राथमिक र द्वितीयक स्रोतबाट सामग्रीको सङ्कलन गरी लेखलाई व्यवस्थित गरिएको छ । यस लेखमा महाभारतकालीन द्वन्द्व, सत्तास्वार्थ तथा कपटपूर्ण व्यवहारहरूको सन्दर्भबाट वर्तमान नेपालको राजनीतिक, सामाजिक अवस्थालाई सम्बद्ध तुल्याइएकाले कृष्ण उपन्यासमा मिथकीय पुनर्लेखनको प्रभावकारी प्रयोग भएको निचोड निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: Shankar Prasad Gaire is a person who writes novels following postmodern thought in the field of Nepali fiction. In this article, an analysis of Shankar Prasad Gaire's novel Krishna has been done on the basis of the mythological theory that is under discussion in the field of Nepali literary criticism in contemporary times. The novel Krishna is a work that looks at a Puranic subject through a modern eye. In the novel, alongside Puranic references, the real state of contemporary society is presented. Studying this on the basis of mythological theory has been considered relevant. Mythological theory is a critical tenet that developed mainly in postmodern times in Western literary thought. It performs the work of searching out and analyzing past subjects and events on the basis of Jung's collective unconscious. Identifying the mythological references used in Shankar Prasad Gaire's novel Krishna is the main problem of this article. The objective of this article is to analyze the novel Krishna with a focus on the mythological concept and to reach a conclusion. Because the work has been analyzed on the basis of mythological theory, the theoretical method of criticism has been used in this article. The novel Krishna is a rewriting of Mahabharata-era narrative. In this novel, the subject matter, characters and their behavior are shown to arise against the background of Puranic story. Because Puranic and supernatural events and references are presented on the basis of contemporary consciousness and events, characters and their tendencies are rewritten, mythological consciousness is seen to have come into the novel in a form favorable to it. The necessary material in this article has been taken from primary and secondary sources. Making mythological reinterpretation and rewriting the theoretical basis, material has been collected from primary and secondary sources as required and the article has been arranged systematically. In this article, by relating the present political and social condition of Nepal to the context of Mahabharata-era conflict, power interests and deceitful behavior, the conclusion is drawn that there has been an effective use of mythological rewriting in the novel Krishna.

informal_english: Shankar Prasad Gaire is a writer who follows postmodern thinking in Nepali fiction, man. In this article, I analyze his novel Krishna using the mythological theory that's been talked about a lot in Nepali literary criticism lately. Krishna is a novel that looks at a Puranic subject through modern eyes. Alongside Puranic references, it presents the real state of contemporary society. Studying it through mythological theory makes sense. Mythological theory is a critical idea that grew up mainly in postmodern times in Western literary thought. It digs into past subjects and events using Jung's collective unconscious. The main problem I tackle is figuring out which mythological references are used in the novel. My goal is to analyze the novel with a focus on mythological ideas and land on a conclusion. Since I'm working from mythological theory, I use the theoretical method of criticism. Krishna is basically a rewriting of a Mahabharata-era story. In it, the subject matter, characters and their behavior grow out of Puranic background. Because Puranic and supernatural events and references are recast through a contemporary lens, events, characters and their tendencies get rewritten, and mythological consciousness shows up in a form that fits the novel. I've drawn the material from primary and secondary sources. Taking mythological reinterpretation and rewriting as my theoretical base, I gathered material from primary and secondary sources as needed and put the article together systematically. In this article, I connect present-day Nepal's political and social condition to Mahabharata-era conflict, power interests and deceitful behavior, and the conclusion I reach is that mythological rewriting is used effectively in the novel Krishna.
